highlights.content: [Skip to content](#content) [![Futurum](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Logo-294x58-1.svg)](https://futurumgroup.com) [Become a Client](https://futurumgroup.com/become-a-client/) [Events](https://futurumgroup.com/insight-type/market-coverage/events/) [Market Coverage](https://futurumgroup.com/insight-type/market-coverage/) ![](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/NP-headshot-no-jacket-cropped-e1725462619126-48x48.jpg) [Nick Patience](https://futurumgroup.com/author/nick-patience/) # Beyond Raw Compute: Equinix’s Strategic Bet on AI Infrastructure * [AI Platforms](https://futurumgroup.com/category/ai-platforms/), [Data Center](https://futurumgroup.com/category/data-center/), [Hybrid Cloud & Infrastructure](https://futurumgroup.com/category/hybrid-cloud-infrastructure/) ![Beyond Raw Compute Equinix’s Strategic Bet on AI Infrastructure](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Beyond-Raw-Compute-Equinixs-Strategic-Bet-on-AI-Infrastructure.png) Analyst(s): Nick Patience Publication Date: September 9, 2026 ## What Is Covered in This Article: * Equinix’s first Horizon customer event and its two flagship launches, Fabric One and Inference Exchange * How NVIDIA and Together AI fit into the Inference Exchange partnership, and who actually owns the GPUs * Why Equinix’s stock has swung from a laggard to one of the AI infrastructure sector’s strongest performers over the past year * What “neutral by design” means as a strategy, and where it runs into limits * How Equinix is pitching sustainability and community investment as part of the same AI buildout story **The Event—Major Themes & Vendor Moves:** Equinix held its first Horizon customer event on September 2 in San Francisco, following an analyst summit the day before, built around two product launches and a keynote pairing CEO Adaire Fox-Martin with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. Fox-Martin traced a lineage of neutral exchanges, from Mesopotamian trade clearing houses through the Athens agora, Amsterdam’s stock exchange, and Wall Street, positioning Equinix as their AI-era equivalent. She cited four forces reshaping enterprise infrastructure: compute fragmenting across an estimated 50 to 70 distinct providers by 2030, network traffic shifting from human-initiated to machine-to-machine, AI token costs becoming a board-level concern, and data sovereignty becoming a design requirement rather than an afterthought. Connecting to each individually, invoking Metcalfe’s Law, means costs that grow geometrically with the number of endpoints, an “AI cloud tax,” Equinix’s connect-once model is built to avoid. Equinix launched two products at the event. Equinix Fabric One is an intent-based connectivity service, built, Equinix says, in five months: customers describe a desired outcome rather than specifying routers, ports, and bandwidth manually, and the network configures itself. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main) [Global](https://www.citybiz.co/city/global/), [New York](https://www.citybiz.co/city/new-york/) [General Business](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/general-business/), [Venture Capital](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/venture-capital/), [Internet / Technology](https://www.citybiz.co/channel/internet-technology/) # Cymphony Launches With $30 Million for AI Agent Security Platform September 9, 2026 ![](https://www.citybiz.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Cymphony.jpg) **Cymphony** has launched with **$30 million** in funding to build an enterprise security and governance platform that tracks how employees and AI agents access sensitive data, interact with corporate systems and create security risks. The funding was co-led by Sequoia Capital and SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund. Cymphony will use the capital to accelerate product development and expand its engineering and go-to-market teams as enterprises deploy more autonomous AI systems across their operations. The New York-based company is targeting an emerging security challenge created by AI agents that can access applications, data and business systems and take actions independently. Cymphony’s thesis is that these agents increasingly need to be governed as participants in an enterprise workforce rather than treated simply as another category of software. The platform gives security teams a unified view of both human employees and AI agents, continuously mapping their identities, system permissions, sensitive data access and interactions across an organization. Cymphony combines SaaS, AI, data and identity signals into a single graph intended to provide business context around those activities. Instead of identifying risk solely through predefined policy violations, the platform analyzes who or what is accessing information, the systems involved and the context surrounding the activity. It then prioritizes identified risks and can recommend or automate remediation. When human intervention is required, Cymphony coordinates the process by identifying the appropriate employees, tracking remediation work and managing security actions through the platform. “The security industry keeps treating AI as another application to secure, but that’s the wrong model to use,” co-founder and CEO **Shy Dekel** said. “AI agents are becoming active participants in the business.” That distinction becomes more significant as companies move from AI assistants that primarily generate information toward autonomous agents capable of completing multi-step workflows across enterprise systems. An agent could potentially interact with a wider combination of applications, data and capabilities than an individual employee typically uses. That creates new questions around permissions, data exposure and accountability, particularly when agents operate across multiple systems to complete a task. Cymphony is positioning its platform as the control layer for that environment. The company has already been adopted by enterprise customers including Syngenta, KKR, Cass Information Systems and Athennian. Its initial customer traction provides Cymphony with operating environments in which to develop its approach as companies determine how autonomous agents should be governed alongside conventional employee identities. The platform also extends established concepts around identity and insider risk into AI-driven workflows. Rather than limiting monitoring to employees and contractors, Cymphony treats agents as additional actors whose permissions, behavior and access relationships need to be understood continuously. “With both human and increasingly agentic threats, insider risk is being redefined in enterprises,” said **Logan Allin**, managing partner at SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund. Cymphony was founded by Shy Dekel, Idan Berkovits and Edi Gotlieb, all graduates of Israel’s Talpiot technology program with backgrounds in cybersecurity, intelligence and engineering. highlights.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # Qualcomm's Amazon AI Chip Deal Offers Momentum, Not a Threat to Nvidia [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Qualcomm has signed a multigenerational agreement to supply Amazon Web Services with custom AI data center chips and optical connectivity, with Amazon receiving warrants for 25 million shares at $161.26 each, a potential $4 billion stake. The deal covers up to $60 billion in purchases over 10 years and focuses on inference workloads, with revenue starting in the December quarter. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon views the agreement as confirming Qualcomm's existing $15 billion fiscal 2029 data center target rather than providing upside, maintaining a Market Perform rating with a $165 price target. By contrast, Rasgon rates Broadcom Outperform after the company projected AI revenue of $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. The partnership marks Qualcomm's second major hyperscaler win after Meta, but does not materially threaten Nvidia's dominance in AI silicon. ##### Key Elements ![Qualcomm's Amazon AI Chip Deal Offers Momentum, Not a Threat to Nvidia](https://img.biggo.com/JKwBbXNNyJHsu3qf4REzwHz38vOJmN9GvLxGb3L7vMI/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzEyYTAwMjA0LWM1NWQtNGMzNS04MTc5LTUzZDA2OGRjNWIyY18xNzg4OTg0MDA5X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Qualcomm has locked in a multigenerational agreement to supply Amazon Web Services with custom AI data center chips and optical connectivity, a deal that validates the smartphone chip giant's push into the infrastructure market but does little to alter the competitive landscape dominated by Nvidia. The partnership, announced September 9, sent Qualcomm shares up 3% as investors digested the terms: Amazon received warrants to acquire 25 million shares at $161.26 apiece, representing a potential $4 billion equity stake, according to a securities filing. The warrants expire September 3, 2036, and vest in tranches tied to commercial milestones and purchases of up to $60 billion in Qualcomm server chips and related technology over a 10-year horizon. The collaboration focuses heavily on inference workloads, the computational process of running AI models after they have been trained. Qualcomm said the effort spans multiple generations of custom silicon aimed at AWS's expanding AI infrastructure, with an emphasis on energy-efficient processing and system-level integration. Revenue from the arrangement is expected to begin in the December quarter. For Qualcomm, the announcement represents a second major hyperscaler endorsement in less than three months. In June, the company unveiled the Dragonfly C1000 data center CPU and said Meta Platforms would adopt the processor when volume production begins in 2028. Qualcomm has set a target of $15 billion in data center revenue for fiscal 2029, a figure management now says it has "very high confidence" in achieving, partly because of the Amazon agreement. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon, who ranks among the top 1% of Wall Street researchers, characterized the deal as confirmation of Qualcomm's existing trajectory rather than evidence of upside beyond current forecasts. After speaking with the company's investor relations team, he concluded the agreement does not appear incremental to the $5 billion fiscal 2027 and $15 billion fiscal 2029 targets already on the books. "This deal may help provide more proof points for current targets (and it sounds like we may get more of them over time), though it appears to be more a clarification on the current trajectory vs providing for upside which may temper reaction for now," Rasgon wrote. By [Kazeem Kasali](https://www.tvcnews.tv/author/tvcn/) September 9, 2026 11:35 PM GMT+1 ![rBT8eRqB](https://www.tvcnews.tv/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/tvcfiller.png) ***Meta has unveiled Muse, a personal artificial intelligence agent designed to move beyond answering questions to independently carrying out tasks on behalf of users.*** The technology, announced by Meta on Tuesday, September 8, represents the company’s latest step in the development of AI systems capable of planning, taking action and adapting to users’ needs rather than simply generating responses. Meta described Muse as a secure and private personal AI agent that can help users manage tasks and long-term goals, while learning from their interactions and preferences. ADVERTISEMENT Unlike conventional AI assistants, Muse is designed to operate across the applications people use daily. It can send emails, book travel, fill out online forms and carry out other tasks, with users able to determine the level of access it receives. “People just tell Muse what needs to get done, and it takes action,” Meta said, adding that the system is powered by Muse Spark, which the company describes as its most capable AI model to date for real-world agentic work. ADVERTISEMENT A key part of the development is Muse Secure VM, a dedicated virtual computer designed to isolate the AI agent, user data and credentials. Meta said a separate security system, known as the Sentinel agent, controls Muse’s access to the internet and can require user approval before sensitive actions are carried out. The company said Muse will also seek users’ approval before actions such as sending emails or making purchases, while providing an audit trail showing what it has done and what it plans to do. ADVERTISEMENT Users will be able to decide which applications Muse can access and what actions it can perform. Meta also said users can disconnect services or opt out of having their interactions used to train its AI models. The system is also designed to retain information that users consider important. ADVERTISEMENT Meta said this could allow Muse to make suggestions based on previous conversations and activities, such as turning a recipe saved on Instagram into a shopping list or remembering dietary requirements when helping to organise a dinner. For online purchases, Muse will initially support checkout through Link, built by Stripe, with Meta saying the system will use one-time payment cards to keep users’ actual card details hidden. Shop Pay and 1Password support are also planned. ADVERTISEMENT Meta said it is developing Muse Confidential VM, expected later this year, which will encrypt the entire virtual machine, including users’ data and conversations, with a key controlled only by the user. The launch marks a broader shift in the AI industry towards agentic AI — systems designed not merely to understand instructions or produce content, but to plan and execute multi-step tasks with limited human intervention. Meta had already begun moving in this direction with its Meta AI assistant, which gained capabilities to create plans, connect to email and calendar applications, conduct research and complete tasks using its Muse Spark model. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/ca/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/ca/) # AMD MI400 Ships With 432GB HBM4 to Challenge Nvidia [2026] * [![Marcus Chen](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/9fd5d0ea0dd03913800acb181fc9c69cee6db42ea45126b6e3b2a3445a6bb2fb?s=50&d=mm&r=g)](https://tech-insider.org/ca/author/marcus-chen/)[Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/ca/author/marcus-chen/ "Posts by Marcus Chen") * [Hardware](https://tech-insider.org/ca/category/hardware/) [Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/ca/author/marcus-chen/) September 9, 2026 14 min read AMD’s newest data center GPU family is now shipping, and the specs make Nvidia’s own roadmap look tight. The **AMD Instinct MI455X**, the flagship of the MI400 series, packs 432GB of HBM4 memory onto a single accelerator, more than 50% above Nvidia’s current Blackwell Ultra B300. That gap, confirmed on AMD’s own product pages and repeated at Hot Chips 2026 in late August, has turned a once-lopsided AI chip market into a genuine two-horse race. For Canadian buyers, cloud operators, and anyone tracking where AI infrastructure dollars are headed in 2026, the AMD MI400 vs Nvidia Rubin contest is no longer theoretical. It is showing up in Toronto data centers, in AMD’s stock price, and in the cost of renting a single GPU by the hour. The launch wasn’t a surprise. AMD previewed the family at CES 2026 in January and gave a technical deep dive at Hot Chips in August, but July’s event marked the point where MI455X moved from slide deck to shipping product for cloud and hyperscale customers. The headline number is memory. Each [MI455X carries 432GB of HBM4](https://www.amd.com/en/products/accelerators/instinct/mi400/mi455x.html), spread across 12 stacks of 36GB each on a 2,048-bit interface, according to AMD’s product page. highlights.content: ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/bigdatawire-logo.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### September 9, 2026 ### September 8, 2026 ### September 4, 2026 ## HP Extends Data-Center AI Architecture to the Edge *Enabling organizations to deploy and manage open, virtualized AI from the data center to the edge with HP ZGX Fury and Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA* PALO ALTO, Calif., Sept. 9, 2026 — [HP Inc.](http://www.hp.com/) today announced a collaboration with Red Hat, the world’s leading provider of open-source solutions, to give organizations more choice in where AI workloads run, whether locally, in the cloud or across both environments. In collaboration with Red Hat, HP is developing an open, enterprise-grade AI platform to deliver purpose-built AI infrastructure powered by Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/09/zgx-fury-press-release-header-300x121.png) HP ZGX Fury, powered by the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, helps organizations bring AI development, inference and orchestration closer to where work happens. HP’s open enterprise-grade AI platform aims to help companies maximize local AI inference throughput with up to 20 PFLOPS FP4 AI performance, reduce environment setup time and deployment risk, and improve GPU utilization through optimized NVIDIA CUDA libraries, scheduling, and multi-GPU workload orchestration. Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA is an integrated AI platform, built on the industry-leading infrastructure of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Red Hat OpenShift, for deploying and managing AI models, agents and applications across the hybrid cloud. The collaboration provides the ability to accelerate AI development by reducing setup time, enabling local agentic coding, and allowing companies to offload compute to the ZGX Fury without altering existing workflows. Running on Red Hat AI Factory, the solution is bringing together the co-engineered and jointly validated power of NVIDIA AI Enterprise and the scalability of Red Hat AI Enterprise. “The future of AI is moving closer to where people work, machines operate and critical decisions are made,” said Jim Nottingham, Senior Vice President and Division President, Advanced Compute and Solutions, HP Inc. “Together with Red Hat and NVIDIA, HP is extending enterprise AI from the data center to the edge with an open, enterprise-grade inference platform designed to give customers greater choice, control and consistency as they deploy local AI factories.” As organizations continue to develop AI solutions requiring AI inference closer to deployment sites, they must address latency, privacy, resiliency, data sovereignty, connectivity and cost. HP intends to help customers move from experimentation to repeatable production deployments with local AI performance and a consistent enterprise software foundation. The platform is being designed to support multiple AI workloads on the same system while maintaining workload isolation, governance, and operational control. This approach can help organizations improve infrastructure utilization and give IT teams a more consistent way to manage distributed AI environments. “Scaling AI from the data center to the edge requires operational consistency and reliability. By powering HP’s platform with Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA, we’re providing the stable, AI-optimized foundation businesses need to bridge the gap between IT and operational technology,” said Ryan King, Vice President, AI and Infrastructure Partner Ecosystem, Red Hat. “We are pleased to collabo...

highlights.titleZh: Nscale, Figure ink US$3.5 billion AI compute deal with NVIDIA GPUs, ETDatacenters
highlights.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 1 minRead # Nscale, Figure ink US$3.5 billion AI compute deal with NVIDIA GPUs AI infrastructure provider Nscale has partnered with humanoid robotics company Figure for a multi-year AI compute deal, initially valued at US$3.5 billion and scalable to over US$6 billion. This collaboration could involve deploying 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs to support Figure's AI models and robots. The agreement highlights increasing demand for high-performance computing infrastructure in the rapidly evolving AI and robotics sectors. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Sep 08, 2026 at 08:50 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Nscale and Figure signed a multi-year AI compute partnership worth US$3.5 billion initially * The deal could lead to the deployment of 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs for Figure's AI models * Initial infrastructure deployment is planned for late 2027 in Barstow, Texas * Nscale will become Figure's preferred compute provider and take a stake in the robotics company [Nscale](/tag/nscale), a provider of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and high-performance graphics processing unit (GPU) cloud services, has signed a multi-year partnership with [Figure](/tag/figure), a humanoid [robotics](/tag/robotics) company. This agreement involves an initial commitment of US$3.5 billion in computing resources, with plans to scale the deal to more than US$6 billion. The partnership is expected to support the deployment of 100,000 [NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) GPUs as Figure expands the computing infrastructure behind its AI models and robots. The planned infrastructure may utilise NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform, the company’s AI computing architecture. Initial deployment is scheduled for the second half of 2027 in Barstow, Texas. ### AI Compute Infrastructure Focus The collaboration will see Nscale become Figure's preferred compute provider and also involve Nscale taking a stake in Figure. The computing infrastructure is designed to support Figure’s Helix AI models, which power its humanoid robots. The companies intend to integrate computing, AI infrastructure, and software across the model development process, from training through deployment. They will also explore the potential use of humanoid robots within Nscale’s own supply chain. Josh Payne, Founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Nscale, highlighted the growth in inference and agentic AI, stating that Figure is pushing the boundaries of AI. Brett Adcock, Founder and CEO of Figure, noted that the expansion of humanoid robots is largely constrained by data and compute, with their AI model, Helix, becoming more capable with increased data and compute. Jensen Huang, Founder and CEO of NVIDIA, commented on the emergence of physical AI through humanoid robots, describing the partnership as activating the robotics flywheel by training Figure’s models on NVIDIA Vera Rubin via Nscale’s AI cloud, validating them in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, and deploying them on NVIDIA GPUs in Figure’s robots. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

highlights.content: [The Rundown AI homepage](/) [University Platform →](https://app.therundown.ai/) Artificial intelligence/News & analysis # Meta introduces Muse as personal AI agents face growing competition Meta’s Muse brings a personal AI agent to WhatsApp and its own app, raising questions about separate agents as OpenAI and Anthropic expand their tools. By Zach Mink··4 min read ![Meta debuts new personal AI agent — newsletter story image](/news/images/4c2e2bdd6972a36002539caf10fd9e158591347f5466213d27e665613b705d72.webp?dpl=dpl_3xhGAdw9KMZbb1L7WK7RNgfma2BP) Image source: Meta Meta has introduced Muse, a personal AI agent that works through a messaging interface and carries out tasks on its own cloud computer. Announced on September 8, Muse can navigate websites, fill out forms, and continue working after a user closes the app, according to [Meta’s launch announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). The launch, covered in [The Rundown’s September 9 newsletter](https://www.therundown.ai/articles/openai-secret-model-settles-a-1m-math-problem), adds another option for people who want to delegate tasks such as booking tables, sending emails, and shopping. It also sharpens a competitive question. As OpenAI and Anthropic bring more agent capabilities into their own assistants, how much room remains for a separate personal agent product? ## How Muse works Meta says users can talk to Muse in its own app or through WhatsApp. Its dedicated cloud computer and browser give it a place to act on requests and keep working in the background. The initial rollout covers U.S. users on iOS, Android, and the web, with free access and paid subscription options, according to the [announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). Muse can also write custom connectors for services that provide an API or command line interface, Meta says. That could expand the services it can reach, although a service still needs to expose a usable interface. Meta’s [technical documentation](https://security.muse.ai/) discusses Gmail access and describes how the system handles credentials and permissions. For tasks involving purchases or sensitive information, Meta says Muse requests approval before sensitive actions. Its architecture separates the working agent from credential storage and a permission authority called Sentinel. Stripe Link payments rely on restricted card credentials that can be used once, alongside purchase approvals, according to [Meta’s security explanation](https://security.muse.ai/). Those safeguards come with qualifications. Meta says it can access data when necessary to operate, secure, or support the service. Sanitized interaction records can be used for training unless users opt out. A stronger Confidential VM protection is planned for later in 2026. Meta also acknowledges that prompt injection remains unsolved, so its security design should be understood as a set of protections with limits. ## Why it matters Muse enters a crowded field of personal agents. The writer’s underlying question is becoming more concrete as frontier providers add tools for browser navigation and agent delegation. If people can assign tasks inside an assistant they already turn to, a separate agent subscription may need a stronger reason to earn their attention and money. OpenAI supplies a direct precedent. On July 17, 2025, it [announced ChatGPT agent](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/) with its own virtual computer, visual and text browsers, a terminal, API access, and connectors. It combined Operator’s website interaction with deep research inside ChatGPT and supported scheduling completed tasks to recur. That announcement shows how a frontier provider can absorb functions that might otherwise justify another product. Anthropic has demonstrated a related direction in research. Its [June 13, 2025 engineering account](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system) de...

The funding was co-led by Sequoia Capital and SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund. Cymphony will use the capital to accelerate product development and expand its engineering and go-to-market teams as enterprises deploy more autonomous AI systems across their operations. The New York-based company is targeting an emerging security challenge created by AI agents that can access applications, data and business systems and take actions independently. Cymphony’s thesis is that these agents increasingly need to be governed as participants in an enterprise workforce rather than treated simply as another category of software. The platform gives security teams a unified view of both human employees and AI agents, continuously mapping their identities, system permissions, sensitive data access and interactions across an organization. Cymphony combines SaaS, AI, data and identity signals into a single graph intended to provide business context around those activities. Instead of identifying risk solely through predefined policy violations, the platform analyzes who or what is accessing information, the systems involved and the context surrounding the activity. It then prioritizes identified risks and can recommend or automate remediation. When human intervention is required, Cymphony coordinates the process by identifying the appropriate employees, tracking remediation work and managing security actions through the platform. “The security industry keeps treating AI as another application to secure, but that’s the wrong model to use,” co-founder and CEO **Shy Dekel** said. “AI agents are becoming active participants in the business.” That distinction becomes more significant as companies move from AI assistants that primarily generate information toward autonomous agents capable of completing multi-step workflows across enterprise systems. An agent could potentially interact with a wider combination of applications, data and capabilities than an individual employee typically uses. That creates new questions around permissions, data exposure and accountability, particularly when agents operate across multiple systems to complete a task. Cymphony is positioning its platform as the control layer for that environment. The company has already been adopted by enterprise customers including Syngenta, KKR, Cass Information Systems and Athennian. Its initial customer traction provides Cymphony with operating environments in which to develop its approach as companies determine how autonomous agents should be governed alongside conventional employee identities. The platform also extends established concepts around identity and insider risk into AI-driven workflows. Rather than limiting monitoring to employees and contractors, Cymphony treats agents as additional actors whose permissions, behavior and access relationships need to be understood continuously. “With both human and increasingly agentic threats, insider risk is being redefined in enterprises,” said **Logan Allin**, managing partner at SMBC Fin Atlas Beyond Fund. By [Kazeem Kasali](https://www.tvcnews.tv/author/tvcn/) September 9, 2026 11:35 PM GMT+1 ![rBT8eRqB](https://www.tvcnews.tv/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/tvcfiller.png) ***Meta has unveiled Muse, a personal artificial intelligence agent designed to move beyond answering questions to independently carrying out tasks on behalf of users.*** The technology, announced by Meta on Tuesday, September 8, represents the company’s latest step in the development of AI systems capable of planning, taking action and adapting to users’ needs rather than simply generating responses. Meta described Muse as a secure and private personal AI agent that can help users manage tasks and long-term goals, while learning from their interactions and preferences. ADVERTISEMENT Unlike conventional AI assistants, Muse is designed to operate across the applications people use daily. It can send emails, book travel, fill out online forms and carry out other tasks, with users able to determine the level of access it receives. “People just tell Muse what needs to get done, and it takes action,” Meta said, adding that the system is powered by Muse Spark, which the company describes as its most capable AI model to date for real-world agentic work. ADVERTISEMENT A key part of the development is Muse Secure VM, a dedicated virtual computer designed to isolate the AI agent, user data and credentials. Meta said a separate security system, known as the Sentinel agent, controls Muse’s access to the internet and can require user approval before sensitive actions are carried out. The company said Muse will also seek users’ approval before actions such as sending emails or making purchases, while providing an audit trail showing what it has done and what it plans to do. ADVERTISEMENT Users will be able to decide which applications Muse can access and what actions it can perform. Meta also said users can disconnect services or opt out of having their interactions used to train its AI models. The system is also designed to retain information that users consider important. ADVERTISEMENT Meta said this could allow Muse to make suggestions based on previous conversations and activities, such as turning a recipe saved on Instagram into a shopping list or remembering dietary requirements when helping to organise a dinner. For online purchases, Muse will initially support checkout through Link, built by Stripe, with Meta saying the system will use one-time payment cards to keep users’ actual card details hidden. Shop Pay and 1Password support are also planned. AI Agents.content: [The Rundown AI homepage](/) [University Platform →](https://app.therundown.ai/) Artificial intelligence/News & analysis # Meta introduces Muse as personal AI agents face growing competition Meta’s Muse brings a personal AI agent to WhatsApp and its own app, raising questions about separate agents as OpenAI and Anthropic expand their tools. By Zach Mink··4 min read ![Meta debuts new personal AI agent — newsletter story image](/news/images/4c2e2bdd6972a36002539caf10fd9e158591347f5466213d27e665613b705d72.webp?dpl=dpl_3xhGAdw9KMZbb1L7WK7RNgfma2BP) Image source: Meta Meta has introduced Muse, a personal AI agent that works through a messaging interface and carries out tasks on its own cloud computer. Announced on September 8, Muse can navigate websites, fill out forms, and continue working after a user closes the app, according to [Meta’s launch announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). The launch, covered in [The Rundown’s September 9 newsletter](https://www.therundown.ai/articles/openai-secret-model-settles-a-1m-math-problem), adds another option for people who want to delegate tasks such as booking tables, sending emails, and shopping. It also sharpens a competitive question. As OpenAI and Anthropic bring more agent capabilities into their own assistants, how much room remains for a separate personal agent product? ## How Muse works Meta says users can talk to Muse in its own app or through WhatsApp. Its dedicated cloud computer and browser give it a place to act on requests and keep working in the background. The initial rollout covers U.S. users on iOS, Android, and the web, with free access and paid subscription options, according to the [announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-personal-ai-agent/). Muse can also write custom connectors for services that provide an API or command line interface, Meta says. That could expand the services it can reach, although a service still needs to expose a usable interface. Meta’s [technical documentation](https://security.muse.ai/) discusses Gmail access and describes how the system handles credentials and permissions. For tasks involving purchases or sensitive information, Meta says Muse requests approval before sensitive actions. Its architecture separates the working agent from credential storage and a permission authority called Sentinel. Stripe Link payments rely on restricted card credentials that can be used once, alongside purchase approvals, according to [Meta’s security explanation](https://security.muse.ai/). Those safeguards come with qualifications. Meta says it can access data when necessary to operate, secure, or support the service. Sanitized interaction records can be used for training unless users opt out. A stronger Confidential VM protection is planned for later in 2026. Meta also acknowledges that prompt injection remains unsolved, so its security design should be understood as a set of protections with limits. ## Why it matters Muse enters a crowded field of personal agents. The writer’s underlying question is becoming more concrete as frontier providers add tools for browser navigation and agent delegation. If people can assign tasks inside an assistant they already turn to, a separate agent subscription may need a stronger reason to earn their attention and money. OpenAI supplies a direct precedent. On July 17, 2025, it [announced ChatGPT agent](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/) with its own virtual computer, visual and text browsers, a terminal, API access, and connectors. It combined Operator’s website interaction with deep research inside ChatGPT and supported scheduling completed tasks to recur. That announcement shows how a frontier provider can absorb functions that might otherwise justify another product. Anthropic has demonstrated a related direction in research. Its [June 13, 2025 engineering account](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system) de...

AI Agents.content: For decades, enterprise software has been designed primarily to record what businesses already know: customer information, financial transactions, employee activity, inventory, sales pipelines, and operational decisions. These platforms became the systems of record that organizations relied on to maintain a consistent version of the truth. Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that model. The emergence of multi-agent AI systems could push enterprise software toward something more dynamic: systems of action that do not simply store information but interpret it, coordinate decisions, and initiate tasks. The shift is significant because enterprise workflows rarely consist of a single question with a single answer. A customer-service issue, for example, may require reviewing account history, checking contractual terms, identifying a potential solution, updating a ticket, and communicating with another department. A single AI assistant can help with individual steps, but coordinating an entire workflow requires something closer to a team of specialized digital workers. That is where multi-agent orchestration enters the picture. For Swaroop Borukar, a seasoned Product Manager building in the AI Infrastructure domain at Workday, this represents a fundamental change in how enterprise applications can be conceived. > Swaroop says, “The real opportunity with multi-agent AI is moving beyond systems that simply answer questions. By giving specialized agents defined responsibilities and the ability to coordinate, enterprises can begin building software that understands a business objective and helps execute the workflow required to achieve it.” ## Why single-agent AI isn’t enough for enterprise workflows The first generation of enterprise generative AI largely focused on the chatbot or copilot model. A user asks a question, the AI retrieves information or generates content, and the user decides what happens next. That approach remains useful, but complex enterprise environments demand more. Modern businesses operate across dozens or even hundreds of interconnected applications. A workflow might span CRM platforms, financial systems, project-management tools, internal databases, and communication applications. Each system has its own permissions, data structures, and business rules. A multi-agent architecture can divide these responsibilities among specialized agents. One agent might retrieve relevant information, another could analyze it, a third could determine what action should be taken, while another validates the proposed action against organizational policies. > “A single general-purpose agent is not always the best architecture for complex enterprise environments,” Swaroop explains. “Specialized agents can be designed around specific functions, permissions, and business rules, making the overall system more controllable, observable, and reliable.” The objective is not simply to have multiple AI models running simultaneously. It is to create an architecture in which agents have defined responsibilities and controlled ways of interacting with one another and with enterprise systems. This distinction is important. Without effective orchestration, adding more agents can create more complexity rather than greater efficiency. For technology leaders, the interesting question is therefore not whether enterprises can connect AI models to their software. It is how they can build an architecture in which autonomous components collaborate reliably enough to participate in real business processes. ## Inside the architecture of a multi-agent enterprise system A well-designed multi-agent system resembles a coordinated organization more than a conventional chatbot. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Edition](/wp-content/themes/tech-edition/assets/images/logo.svg)](https://www.techedt.com/) [AI](/tag/ai)[Cybersecurity](/tag/cybersecurity)[Data Centres](/tag/data-centres)[Start-ups](/tag/startups)[NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) [Home](https://www.techedt.com/)/[Business](https://www.techedt.com/category/business) Business # Meta rolls out Muse AI agent in the US to handle tasks across the web Built on Muse Spark, Meta's new AI agent completes web errands, remembers user preferences and executes secure payments inside an isolated virtual machine. ![Nurin Sofia](https://techedt.gumlet.io/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Nurin-Sofia.jpg?compress=true) **[Nurin Sofia](https://www.techedt.com/author/nurin-sofia)**9 September 2026 · 4 min read [![](https://www.techedt.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google.svg)Add as a preferred **source on Google**](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=techedt.com)[![](/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/news.svg)Follow us on **Google News**](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqJQgKIh9DQklTRVFnTWFnMEtDM1JsWTJobFpIUXVZMjl0S0FBUAE?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen) ![Meta rolls out Muse AI agent in the US to handle tasks across the web](https://www.techedt.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Meta-rolls-out-Muse-AI-agent-in-the-US-to-handle-tasks-across-the-web-1440x810.jpg) Meta has begun rolling out Muse, a personal artificial intelligence assistant designed to execute everyday web activities on behalf of users. The tool can manage a broad spectrum of responsibilities, including booking travel arrangements, filling out digital forms, handling purchases and sending emails. Accessible through both WhatsApp and a dedicated Muse application, the software is powered by Muse Spark, an engine Meta identifies as its most capable foundation model to date. People can assign the agent an immediate chore or an overarching goal, prompting it to devise the requisite sequence of steps autonomously. Once tasked, Muse is able to launch an internal browser and interact smoothly across various connected online services to fulfil the user’s instructions. ## Muse can keep working after the app is closed The assistant caters to both quick, one-off assignments and complex projects that require extended time to resolve. By designing a personalised roadmap tailored to a specific goal, it coordinates the necessary schedule and resources, proceeding with its work even after someone closes the application. Within its dedicated web browser, Muse can research sites, submit completed forms and negotiate terms on behalf of the account holder. Should external circumstances shift or pivotal moments arise, the software pauses to consult the individual before proceeding. Crucially, sensitive undertakings such as dispatching an email or executing a transaction will always require explicit confirmation from the user. A persistent memory system allows the agent to retain and transfer relevant context between disparate conversations and activities. For instance, Meta explains that Muse can transform a recipe saved on Instagram into an organised shopping list while actively recalling the dietary preferences of guests invited to a dinner party. It subsequently applies such background knowledge to offer helpful suggestions unprompted, though users always retain full authority to command the system to purge specific retained memories. Financial transactions are processed through Link by Stripe, which issues single-use virtual cards to ensure private payment information remains concealed from the AI. This arrangement makes Muse the first autonomous agent backed by Link purchase protection guarantees, offering safeguards against damaged goods, lost shipments, unexpected price reductions and return fees. Meta also intends to broaden these financial options by integrating Shop Pay as an additional payment method. LLMs.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # The AGI race heats up: Can MiniMax's omni-modal approach outrun the giants? [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) In early September 2026, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra and declared "welcome to the AGI era," followed by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's assertion that AGI has arrived—yet the industry still lacks consensus on what AGI actually means or how to measure it. Chinese large-model vendors have been comparatively restrained in their update cadence. MiniMax, a leading proponent of the omni-modal approach, has seen its video model H3 top certain leaderboards, but its large language model M3 has failed to crack the first tier in either domestic or international benchmarks. The company's revenue mix is shifting from consumer to enterprise, and while its low-price strategy has driven scale, it continues to squeeze profitability—adjusted net loss widened 111.2% year-over-year in the first half of 2026. MiniMax's stock has recovered modestly after plunging roughly 85% from a peak market cap of about HK$410 billion (approximately $52.3 billion). Founder Yan Junjie has set AGI as the point where AI contributes 2% to societal GDP, but the company remains far from that goal. ##### Key Elements ![The AGI race heats up: Can MiniMax's omni-modal approach outrun the giants?](https://img.biggo.com/cLB4TO3L-RLcPhD0mF_FMCRhEOYDbaNbVbRiJkuL-Gw/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzM1NWQ3NzRjLWEyOTgtNGM2NS1hMjQ0LTA3MmMxNzI4MzA3NF8xNzg5MDAxOTk4X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) In early September 2026, the global AI industry saw a dense wave of model releases. Anthropic, Meta, Google, and OpenAI rolled out flagship new models within a span of just three days. OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman went further at the GPT-6 Astra launch, declaring "welcome to the AGI era." AGI—Artificial General Intelligence—refers to AI that can understand the world like a human, reason autonomously, and flexibly handle complex cross-domain tasks. GPT-6 Astra can simulate human vision by reading screen pixels directly, operating any software with a graphical interface via mouse and keyboard, and chaining reasoning, code execution, visual recognition, computer operation, and tool invocation into a single execution pipeline—autonomously planning and completing end-to-end workflows. This already begins to meet the definition of highly autonomous AGI. Yet whether AGI has truly arrived is far from settled. Shortly before GPT-6 Astra's release, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had described AGI as "a wildly vague term." The ARC Prize team, which conducted key evaluations of GPT-6 Astra, also cautioned that while the model represents meaningful progress in generalization, "we are not claiming it is AGI." ### Overseas giants race to declare AGI; Chinese players move at a measured pace In contrast to the high-profile declarations from overseas giants, Chinese large-model vendors were relatively restrained in their early-September update cadence. Alibaba updated Qwen3.8-Max on September 2, and iFlytek released Spark X2.5 on September 7. Another China-related development: HUMAIN, an AI company under Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, launched the world's first Arabic large language model on September 3, post-trained on MiniMax's open-source M3 model. MiniMax is one of the earliest movers in China's large-model space. Founded in late 2021, it released its first text model, abab1, in April 2022—seven months before OpenAI launched ChatGPT. The company did not confine itself to a single modality, instead developing text, speech, video, and music models in parallel, aiming to approach AGI faster through omni-modal fusion. LLMs.title: Cortico Launches Benchmark to Test Clinical AI Safety
LLMs.titleZh: Cortico Launches Benchmark to Test Clinical AI Safety
LLMs.content: * [Skip to primary navigation](#genesis-nav-primary) * [Skip to primary sidebar](#genesis-sidebar-primary) # Cortico Launches Benchmark to Test Clinical AI Safety by [Techcouver Newsdesk](https://techcouver.com/author/techcouver-newsdesk/) [Leave a Comment](https://techcouver.com/2026/09/09/cortico-launches-benchmark-to-test-clinical-ai-safety/#respond) ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) Vancouver healthcare technology company [Cortico](https://cortico.health/) has launched a free, open benchmark designed to measure whether artificial intelligence models can safely support clinical decisions—not merely pass medical exams. Called [MedSafe-Dx](https://msdx.cortico.health/), the benchmark evaluates how large language models respond when a patient may require urgent care, when reassurance could be dangerous, and when the available information warrants uncertainty. Across 11 frontier models evaluated in its launch paper, Cortico found that even the strongest performers faced a significant trade-off between safety and usefulness. The model with the highest safety pass rate, GPT-5.2, passed 97.6% of cases but escalated 71% of routine cases. At the other end, the poorest performer missed 26 of 156 cases classified as urgent. “High accuracy often masks dangerous overconfidence,” said Cortico CEO and co-founder Clark Van Oyen. “We built MedSafe-Dx to give clinicians and health systems transparent, verifiable safety metrics.” MedSafe-Dx tests three behaviours: whether a model escalates potentially life-threatening cases, avoids falsely reassuring patients who may be at risk, and expresses appropriate uncertainty when symptoms are ambiguous. The evaluation presented 250 simulated adult patient cases from the DDXPlus dataset to models developed by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and DeepSeek. Rather than relying on another AI model to judge the responses, MedSafe-Dx uses deterministic rules, frozen datasets and standardized outputs intended to make results reproducible and auditable. The benchmark revealed that diagnostic accuracy did not necessarily translate into safer recommendations. Gemini 3 Pro Preview recorded the highest Top-3 diagnostic recall at 87.2%, according to Cortico, but the lowest safety pass rate at 62.4%. Every model evaluated missed at least some cases categorized as requiring escalation. The findings point to a difficult balance for healthcare AI developers. Models that escalate nearly every questionable case may avoid some dangerous misses, but excessive warnings can burden clinical resources and eventually be ignored—a problem already familiar to providers using electronic health record alerts. Cortico has since expanded the [live leaderboard](https://msdx.cortico.health/) to 12 models from six AI labs, adding models from Meta and xAI. The company has also made the benchmark’s code and dataset publicly available alongside a [medRxiv preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.14.26350711). Cortico stresses that MedSafe-Dx is a comparative safety test, not a clinical validation study or evidence that any model is ready for deployment. Its cases are simulated, while escalation labels are derived from dataset severity ratings rather than assessments by practising clinicians. Still, the company argues that health systems evaluating AI should demand safety testing that examines judgment, confidence and escalation behaviour—not rely solely on exam-style accuracy scores. LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # Mercury 2.5 vs Gemini Diffusion: LLMs Hit 10x Speed [2026] * [![Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/)[Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/ "Posts by Elias Virtanen") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/) September 9, 2026 21 min read OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra can write a working script, but you will wait for it to type every token, one at a time, the way it has since the original GPT-3. Inception Labs’ Mercury 2.5 does not type. It sketches an entire answer in rough form, then refines the whole thing in parallel passes, the same way a Stable Diffusion image goes from noise to a finished picture. Diffusion language models spent 2024 and 2025 as a research curiosity. In September 2026 they are a live purchasing decision, with a general-availability API, real pricing, and a growing list of production use cases at companies that need speed more than they need the last few points of reasoning accuracy. Every mainstream chatbot you have used, from GPT-6 Astra to Claude to Gemini’s Flash and Pro lines, is autoregressive. A 2,000-token answer takes roughly twice as long as a 1,000-token one, no matter how fast the underlying hardware is, because each token depends on every token before it. It starts with a masked or noisy version of the full output and refines the entire sequence over a small number of parallel steps, gradually replacing noise with real tokens across the whole answer at once. LLMs.titleZh: OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra is an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities
LLMs.content: # OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra is an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities — company warns of alignment challenges as new frontier leader emerges Meanwhile, low-cost, intelligent-enough solutions are exploding in popularity. "AI is grown, more than designed," OpenAI's chief scientist, Jakub Pachocki, said in a new blog post on the company's latest GPT-6 Astra release. Titling the piece "An Alien Mind," Pachocki portrays the latest large language model as something more ethereal and harder to quantify. Jensen Huang calls it AGI, and OpenAI claims it's the best, most aligned model the company has ever released. It's safer to delegate, better at complex work tasks, and it can even beat Portal in just a few hours. Huang also said that AGI had previously been achieved back in March earlier this year. Artificial Analysis benchmarks suggest Astra is about as smart as Fable 5.1 - though crucially, cheaper on a per-task basis. Astra may well be better aligned than models in the past, and it may well be more capable in specific tasks and specific benchmarks. However, the claims that the model has achieved AGI, or Artificial General Intelligence, suggest an inflection point for the AI industry. Astra's release comes alongside calls for an industry slowdown, greater government oversight, and controls on the AI industry. Now, OpenAI's Astra raises more eyebrows about frontier-level intelligence. ## Trust us, we don't know what we're doing The tone around OpenAI's Astra release is intriguing. OpenAI's produced a new set of benchmarks, touting bold claims about the model's reasoning capabilities, with the model trained on 100,000 Blackwell GPUs, with more coming soon. But Pachocki's blog post is much more nebulous. While Huang touts that AGI has arrived publicly, Pachocki says AI can only ever "simulate facets of human behaviour," not recreate it. He describes AI development as an experimental process that often "surprises" developers, with results that are "harder to interpret." "An aligned AI should act with honesty and integrity, with love for humanity," Pachocki said. He speaks a lot on alignment, and it's encouraging that OpenAI is so keen to embed human moral understanding into its developments. Although OpenAI appears to be doing this more by orienting the model's goals towards a moralistic outcome, rather than helping to intrinsically understand human morality. It's certainly different to the tack taken by other AI developers, where the likes of xAI's Grok was released with the ability to generate harmful content. But the timing of Pachocki's warning is a little suspect. OpenAI has faced increasing pressure of late for its models to be more affordable, with Chinese alternatives like Deepseek V4, Kimi K3, as well as Western models like Google's Gemini Flash 3.8 and Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 offering compelling levels of intelligence at a much more affordable price than the frontier models. It's perhaps telling that even for all its intelligence and alignment pre-training, GPT 6 Astra is notably cheaper to run on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index than its chief rival, Anthropic's Fable 5.1 — which still retains the top spot on that Intelligence Index at the time of writing. Though it's 50% more expensive than GPT 5.6 Sol on the same tasks. ## It's a researcher, but imagine what it could be A huge component of marketing from the major AI developers has consistently been grounded in the idea that, as good as the models are now, just imagine how capable they're going to be in the future. This was very much the underlying tone in Pachocki's breakdown of Astra's design and functions. Although he and OpenAI make broad suggestions about intelligence, and that the likes of Astra could be this new kind of intelligence which we don't really understand but can definitely control and corral, Pachocki ends his post by making it very clear that we aren't there yet. LLMs.titleZh: Can AI Predict What Humans Do and Why? USC Study Sheds Light on AI’s Limits
LLMs.content: [![Image](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/USC-Shield-BlackBG.png)](https://usc.edu/) [![Formal](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Formal-Viterbi-Logo-New.png)](/) --- [School of Engineering](/) # Can AI Predict What Humans Do and Why? USC Study Sheds Light on AI’s Limits Venice Tang | September 9, 2026  USC AI researcher and robotics pioneer find that LLMs can make human-like predictions by observing players in social games but struggle to learn from experience and apply what they learn to new situations ![Illustration of an AI agent playing chess (Credit: Midjourney)](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/1200-x-600-article-feature-photos-22.png) AI predicting human motivation and behaviors by watching people play games (Credit: Midjourney) A new USC study examined whether large language models (LLMs) could reason about human behavior in strategic social situations, using simple social games to test how well the models could predict players’ actions and motives. Led by USC robotics pioneer engineer [Maja Matarić](https://viterbi.usc.edu/directory/faculty/Mataric/Maja) and her PhD student [Kaleen Shrestha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kaleen-shrestha/), the study evaluates whether today’s AI models can recognize underlying human motives, learn from behavior over time and apply that knowledge to new situations. The study tests AI’s capabilities by having the models observe people playing different social games and predict players’ next moves based on their previous actions, while also attempting to identify each player’s motives. The research team also compares AI predictions with human predictions, making it the first study to evaluate AI reasoning skills over time and compare these “temporal” results with human performance in a game context to date. Started in fall 2024, the project resulted in the paper titled “[Can Large Language Models Infer Human Actions and Motives? Evaluation in Social Prediction and Inspection Games](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1641.pdf).” The paper was accepted to the [2026 Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL) conference](https://2026.aclweb.org/). [Matarić](https://viterbi.usc.edu/directory/faculty/Mataric/Maja) is a Chan Soon-Shiong Chair and Distinguished Professor of Computer Science, Neuroscience, and Pediatrics at [USC Viterbi School of Engineering](https://viterbi.usc.edu/) and the [USC Mark and Mary Stevens School of Computing and AI](https://stevens-computing-ai.usc.edu/)‘s [Thomas Lord Department of Computer Science](https://www.cs.usc.edu/). She also has a joint appointment at the [Department of Pediatrics at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles](https://www.chla.org/department-pediatrics). ## Putting AI to the Test “Games have historically been a good way to poke into the human psyche, understand human behavioral patterns and investigate or infer human motivations in social experiments and studies,” said Shrestha. She emphasizes that showing AI how humans play a game is a key way to evaluate AI’s ability to engage in strategic reasoning based on its observations. To test AI’s ability, her team built on existing cognitive science literature and economic game theories, and adopted two frameworks in the experiment: Social Prediction Game (SPG) and Inspection Game (IG). The study tested common AI models like ChatGPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Llama models. SPG is designed to test an LLM’s ability to predict the actions of a simulated opponent based on observed history. AI observers watched human players play 16 rounds of four different classic economic games, including the Prisoner’s Dilemma, Stag Hunt, Harmony Game and Snowdrift Game. After every round, the models were asked to predict whether “player A” would cooperate or defect in the next round based on the player’s previous actions. Researchers also varied Player A’s underlying motive. Some players were programmed with human-li...

The group operates within the existing Accenture Google Business Group and pairs Accenture's Gemini-certified engineers and industry consultants with specialized Google Cloud technical staff. At the center of the initiative is a dedicated workforce of 1,000 forward-deployed engineers, a role first popularized by Palantir that has become one of the most sought-after positions in tech. Postings for the job have surged more than 700% over the past year, according to market data. These engineers work inside client companies, integrating AI into existing workflows and customizing tools for specific business needs rather than delivering software from a distance. AI Product.content: For decades, enterprise software has been designed primarily to record what businesses already know: customer information, financial transactions, employee activity, inventory, sales pipelines, and operational decisions. These platforms became the systems of record that organizations relied on to maintain a consistent version of the truth. Artificial intelligence is beginning to challenge that model. The emergence of multi-agent AI systems could push enterprise software toward something more dynamic: systems of action that do not simply store information but interpret it, coordinate decisions, and initiate tasks. The shift is significant because enterprise workflows rarely consist of a single question with a single answer. A customer-service issue, for example, may require reviewing account history, checking contractual terms, identifying a potential solution, updating a ticket, and communicating with another department. A single AI assistant can help with individual steps, but coordinating an entire workflow requires something closer to a team of specialized digital workers. That is where multi-agent orchestration enters the picture. For Swaroop Borukar, a seasoned Product Manager building in the AI Infrastructure domain at Workday, this represents a fundamental change in how enterprise applications can be conceived. > Swaroop says, “The real opportunity with multi-agent AI is moving beyond systems that simply answer questions. By giving specialized agents defined responsibilities and the ability to coordinate, enterprises can begin building software that understands a business objective and helps execute the workflow required to achieve it.” ## Why single-agent AI isn’t enough for enterprise workflows The first generation of enterprise generative AI largely focused on the chatbot or copilot model. A user asks a question, the AI retrieves information or generates content, and the user decides what happens next. That approach remains useful, but complex enterprise environments demand more. Modern businesses operate across dozens or even hundreds of interconnected applications. A workflow might span CRM platforms, financial systems, project-management tools, internal databases, and communication applications. Each system has its own permissions, data structures, and business rules. A multi-agent architecture can divide these responsibilities among specialized agents. One agent might retrieve relevant information, another could analyze it, a third could determine what action should be taken, while another validates the proposed action against organizational policies. > “A single general-purpose agent is not always the best architecture for complex enterprise environments,” Swaroop explains. “Specialized agents can be designed around specific functions, permissions, and business rules, making the overall system more controllable, observable, and reliable.” The objective is not simply to have multiple AI models running simultaneously. It is to create an architecture in which agents have defined responsibilities and controlled ways of interacting with one another and with enterprise systems. This distinction is important. Without effective orchestration, adding more agents can create more complexity rather than greater efficiency. For technology leaders, the interesting question is therefore not whether enterprises can connect AI models to their software. It is how they can build an architecture in which autonomous components collaborate reliably enough to participate in real business processes. ## Inside the architecture of a multi-agent enterprise system A well-designed multi-agent system resembles a coordinated organization more than a conventional chatbot. Open Source AI.content: UPDATED 18:27 EDT / SEPTEMBER 09 2026 ### Harvey raises another $550M to develop AI tools for legal teams Six months after its last nine-figure funding round, Harvey AI Corp. today announced that it has raised $550 million at $15.5 billion valuation. Diffusion and Lightspeed Venture Partners led the deal. They were joined by more than a dozen other backers including Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins and Goldman Sachs. Harvey sells a cloud platform that law firms use to automate manual work for their attorneys. The company says that its installed base includes 80% of the 100 highest-ranked law firms in the U.S. Harvey is also popular among large enterprises’ in-house legal teams: it counts half the Fortune 10 as customers. The company’s platform enables users to store up to 100,000 documents in a repository called Vault. A built-in search engine uses artificial intelligence to surface useful patterns. For example, an attorney could ask Harvey to find supplier contracts that must be modified to comply with a new regulation. The process of drafting a new legal document often requires lawyers to review their company’s existing agreements. For example, an attorney might scan historical customer contracts to find clauses that should be included in an important new deal. Harvey’s AI helps users find relevant documents in Vault. It also retrieves external data such as precedents and legislative clauses. Earlier this year, Harvey rolled out AI agents that enable users to automate more complex tasks. An investment firm, for example, could use the agents to find potential issues in a large collection of due diligence documents. Harvey’s agents ask attorneys for input when they need clarification about a tricky part of a task. Today’s funding milestone comes a few days after the company debuted its first custom large language model. Tenet is a fine-tuned version of Kimi K3, an open-source LLM with 2.8 trillion parameters. It comprises 896 individual neural networks that are each optimized for a different set of tasks. Harvey fine-tuned Tenet by training it on legal documents. It also added a custom harness, a collection of prompts and other technical assets designed to optimize LLM output quality. Harvey says that Tenet performs some contract processing tasks 20% better than Kimi K3. Furthermore, it outperforms Fable 5 and GPT-5 Sol in multiple areas. Harvey stated in Tenet’s launch blog post that it plans to deploy more computing infrastructure to advance its AI research. In particular, the company will prioritize the development of “new generalist models.” Today’s funding round should make it easier for Harvey to shoulder the steep costs associated with custom model development. Training custom LLMs could not only help the company differentiate its feature set but also boost its margins. Developing a proprietary model is expensive, but it can lower infrastructure costs in the long term by reducing the need to use external models. The reason is that inference usually accounts for a much bigger percentage of an AI workload’s cost than training. Harvey debuted Tenet alongside LAB, a benchmark that measures LLMs’ ability to complete legal work. The current iteration of the evaluation includes about 1,200 tasks. Open Source AI.content: **[Help Net Security newsletters](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)**: Daily and weekly news, cybersecurity jobs, open source projects, breaking news – **[subscribe here!](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)** Please turn on your JavaScript for this page to function normally. ![Mirko Zorz](https://img.helpnetsecurity.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/12/09195720/avatar-mirko-100x100.jpg) [Mirko Zorz](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/mirkozorz/ "Author archive: https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/mirkozorz/"), Director of Content, Help Net Security **Share** # AI-Infra-Guard: Open-source security scanner for AI systems Tencent’s Zhuque Lab built AI-Infra-Guard, an open-source security scanner for [AI systems](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/02/becky-palmer-national-life-group-ai-driven-cyber-threats/). It fingerprints running services such as Ollama, vLLM and ComfyUI and checks them against more than 1,600 known CVEs, inspects MCP servers and agent skills across 14 categories of risk, and runs jailbreak evaluations against a target model. To check a skill, the platform asks a language model whether it looks malicious. Zhuque Lab scores that call against SkillTrustBench, a public set of 5,520 human-labeled samples across nine risk categories. False positive rates there run from 1.20 percent to 18.67 percent, depending on which model does the judging. The model a team plugs in decides how much reading they end up doing. At the low end, about one clean skill in eighty gets flagged. At the high end, close to one flag in five is a waste of somebody’s afternoon. Banks, carriers and manufacturers use the tool, including ICBC, China Merchants Bank, China Telecom, Lenovo, vivo and Bilibili. Zhuque Lab splits the platform into two layers, and only one of them involves interpretation. “CVE version-matching isn’t intent-based at all,” the AI-Infra-Guard team said. “FPR there is purely a function of fingerprint accuracy.” ### The scanner reads files an attacker wrote Both scanning components ingest tool descriptions and skill files that a hostile server controls. [Indirect prompt injection](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/04/24/indirect-prompt-injection-in-the-wild/) is the technique that exploits this: instructions buried in content the model reads, aimed at the model doing the reading. Release 4.1.9 hardened the scanning agents against it. “File/tool content that gets read is placed into a dedicated, explicitly-delimited text block in the prompt, structurally separated from instructions, rather than mixed inline. The scanning agent is told to treat that block as data to analyze, never as commands to follow,” the team told Help Net Security. The move “cuts naive-to-moderate injection significantly,” but “it’s a mitigation, not a formal guarantee,” and “we don’t claim it’s unbreakable, and we’d say that about any LLM-driven agent.” A defender scanning a suspicious MCP server should treat a clean result as one input, not a clearance. ### No login in the open-source build The repository carries a warning against putting the platform on the internet: it “currently lacks an authentication mechanism.” A scanner built to tell an organization which of its AI services are exposed comes with instructions not to expose the scanner. “AI-Infra-Guard is a single-operator tool by design,” the team said. “No login, no RBAC.” Zhuque Lab’s answer is to put the access control outside the application: “the documented recommendation is a reverse proxy in front (nginx with Basic Auth or an IP allowlist) plus normal firewall rules.” That is the login layer. A team that skips it is running a vulnerability scanner that holds the API keys for every model it evaluates, reachable by anyone who can route to the port. AI-Infra-Guard is available for free on [GitHub](https://github.com/Tencent/AI-Infra-Guard). **Must read:** * [20 open-source cybersecurity tools to keep your team ready for anything](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/202...

Trained at immense compute costs, these open-weight or closed models serve as decision engines for multi-step workflows, software refactoring and risk analysis. The word “frontier” makes [artificial intelligence](https://builtin.com/artificial-intelligence) sound like a territory on a map. It isn’t. The term describes as expensive, moving boundary. A [model](https://builtin.com/articles/ai-models) that once felt astonishing can quickly become everyday [software](https://builtin.com/tag/software) running on a modest [cloud](https://builtin.com/cloud-computing) instance or a developer’s laptop. The frontier simply describes whatever systems currently sit at the leading edge of what AI can do. That makes frontier AI different from a stable category like a database or an operating system. It is an empirical description of a threshold that refuses to sit still. ## What Is a Frontier AI Model? Frontier AI refers to the moving, leading-edge boundary of artificial intelligence, describing systems capable of handling ambiguous, high-complexity tasks that simpler models cannot solve. Rather than a fixed category, it represents an empirical threshold defined by what a model can actually do: multi-step reasoning, writing functional code and evaluating risk across complex documents. More From Richard Ewing[Who’s Actually Responsible for Your AI Agents?](https://builtin.com/articles/who-governs-ai-agent) ## Everyday AI vs. Frontier AI Most artificial intelligence running inside businesses today is built for predictable, narrow work. Everyday AI includes the spam filters catching [phishing](https://builtin.com/articles/phishing-attacks) attempts in your inbox, [recommendation engines](https://builtin.com/data-science/recommendation-engine) ranking media feeds, transcription tools turning speech into text and small models tuned to categorize customer service tickets. The release candidate added a check for pull requests that contain AI-generated code that no person has reviewed. The check sits inside AGENTS.md, a file in the systemd repository that gives instructions to AI coding agents working on the project. It tells any agent modifying source files to add two lines at the top of README.md before starting other work. One line reads: "Remove this line to confirm you've reviewed this PR before submitting." The agent cannot remove either line on its own. Only the human author of the pull request can delete them before the change merges. NetworkManager, a separate open-source networking project, added a comparable check to its own AGENTS.md file earlier this year. systemd 262-rc2 also corrected an off-by-one read error in the tar-util code. It added an option to disable the systemd-coredumpd service and synchronized the codebase against updated Linux kernel headers and syscall lists. Documentation received updates, and the hardware database gained an entry for the MacBookAir9,1 T2 touchpad. systemd 262-rc2 became [available for testing on GitHub](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/releases/tag/v262-rc2) the same day. Linux kernel policy requires a person to review and sign off on every AI-assisted change before it merges into the tree. Linus Torvalds addressed the pace of AI-found fixes after [Linux 7.2-rc7 landed August 9, 2026](https://betanews.com/article/linux-7-2-rc7-ai-review-new-normal/), with more than 400 patches from over 230 contributors. In July, Torvalds told developers who objected to AI tools in kernel development that they could fork the project or leave it. He wrote, "Linux is not one of those anti-AI projects." [Linux 7.3-rc2 shipped September 7, 2026](https://betanews.com/article/linux-7-3-rc2-torvalds-ai-blame/), heavier than usual, with fixes spread across networking, graphics, and filesystems. Torvalds attributed the size to a missed EDAC pull request, a busy DRM merge, and AI. Linux kernel policy requires a person to review and sign off on every AI-assisted change before it merges into the tree. Torvalds attributed the size to a missed EDAC pull request, a busy DRM merge, and AI.
