Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # Mercury 2.5 vs Gemini Diffusion: LLMs Hit 10x Speed [2026] * [![Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/)[Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/ "Posts by Elias Virtanen") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Elias Virtanen](https://tech-insider.org/author/elias-virtanen/) September 9, 2026 21 min read OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra can write a working script, but you will wait for it to type every token, one at a time, the way it has since the original GPT-3. Inception Labs’ Mercury 2.5 does not type. It sketches an entire answer in rough form, then refines the whole thing in parallel passes, the same way a Stable Diffusion image goes from noise to a finished picture. The result, according to Inception’s own September 8, 2026 launch numbers, is **1,107 tokens per second** on widely available Nvidia GPUs, a pace no mainstream autoregressive model comes close to matching in production. This is a comparison most buyers’ guides have skipped because the technology only became commercially credible in the past few months. Diffusion language models spent 2024 and 2025 as a research curiosity. In September 2026 they are a live purchasing decision, with a general-availability API, real pricing, and a growing list of production use cases at companies that need speed more than they need the last few points of reasoning accuracy. This article puts Mercury 2.5 next to Google’s still-experimental Gemini Diffusion and OpenAI’s flagship autoregressive model, GPT-6 Astra, using published specs, independent benchmark data, and real pricing pages, so you can decide whether a diffusion LLM belongs in your stack. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What Is a Diffusion LLM, and Why Does It Change the Speed Math? Every mainstream chatbot you have used, from GPT-6 Astra to Claude to Gemini’s Flash and Pro lines, is autoregressive. It predicts the next token, appends it, then predicts the next one after that, one at a time, left to right. That is why streaming responses appear to type themselves out: the model genuinely is generating them in that order. It is also why latency scales with output length. A 2,000-token answer takes roughly twice as long as a 1,000-token one, no matter how fast the underlying hardware is, because each token depends on every token before it. A diffusion LLM works the way an image diffusion model works. It starts with a masked or noisy version of the full output and refines the entire sequence over a small number of parallel steps, gradually replacing noise with real tokens across the whole answer at once. Zylos AI’s June 2026 research note on diffusion models for agentic inference describes it as “less typewriter, more editor revising a full draft at once.” Because many tokens get resolved in each pass instead of one token per forward pass, output speed becomes far less tied to answer length, and a single GPU can push a lot more tokens per second than an autoregressive model of similar quality. The tradeoff is not free. Diffusion models generally need more careful training to reach the same reasoning depth as a comparable autoregressive model, and the field is younger, so the biggest labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google’s flagship Gemini line) still ship autoregressive transformers as their primary prod...

Open Source AI.content: ![Redhat Developers Logo](/themes/custom/rhdp_fe/images/branding/Logo-Red_Hat_Developer-A-Reverse-RGB.svg) ### Get started with AI ### Featured resources ### Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA ### Self-guided ### Hands-on ### Browse by topic ### Training & certifications ### Get started ### Download products ### Featured ### References ### Get involved ### Follow along ### Get help ### Join the Red Hat Developer program # Use a local and open source code assistant There's a lot of excitement about AI coding assistants, but many of the available options either aren't open source, or don't respect your data privacy by sending what you're working on to the cloud for processing. If you're looking for an alternative to closed AI, then you need an open coding assistant and an open source IDE. The [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) project provides you with an open source AI coding assistant using the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it can be used with most text editors, including VS Code or Cursor, or as a standalone command-line interface. ## What is OpenCode? OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent. It can be used as a terminal-based interface, a desktop application, or as an IDE extension. You install OpenCode on your computer, so it can run locally with no internet connection. OpenCode is the software providing an interface for you to access an LLM. It's not an LLM itself, so there are a few different components you must install. This kind of modularity is good, though, because it gives you the choice to use any LLM (even one that's private to your organization, or one that requires a paid subscription). ## Install OpenCode First, you must install OpenCode itself. This provides a terminal-based chat interface, and the software that gets run for MCP connections. On Linux, install using `curl` and Bash: `curl` `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash` On MacOS, install using the `brew` command from the [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) project: `brew` `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode` On Windows, install using the `choco` command from the [Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org/) project: `choco` `choco install opencode` ## Install an LLM Now that OpenCode has been installed, you need an LLM to actually process queries and formulate probable responses. OpenCode provides an LLM by default, but it is not an open source one. If you're happy to use a proprietary LLM that sends your data to someone else's cloud, then you can skip down to the [Integrate OpenCode with your editor](#integrate) section, bypassing the installation and configuration of an open LLM. I don't recommend this, because the LLM that OpenCode provides does not keep your data private, and its no-cost access could potentially end. There are a few good open source LLMs to choose from, and the one you use is likely to be determined by your use case and your available resources. At Red Hat, the adage is that local AI is a race car, and Red Hat AI is a bullet train. With a local AI, you can go fast with just a few passengers, but with a bullet train you can go even faster with lots of passengers. For local development, it makes sense to use local AI tools, like Ollama or OpenVINO. In summary: To find out what graphic processor your computer uses, go to your desktop's system settings and search for "GPU" or "graphics processor". For example, in the GNOME desktop for Linux, launch **Settings**, click **System** in the left column, and then **About** > **System Details** (figure 1). ![GNOME System Details window listing system hardware, showing Intel Graphics (ARL) under the Graphics entry.](/sites/default/files/styles/article_floated/public/figure-1_43.png?itok=oFJ3NzVp) ## Ollama for AMD and NVIDIA The [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) project is an open source AI platform that lets you download and run large language models locally, on your own computer. Infra & Chips.content: [Skip to content](#content) [![Futurum](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Logo-294x58-1.svg)](https://futurumgroup.com) [Become a Client](https://futurumgroup.com/become-a-client/) [Events](https://futurumgroup.com/insight-type/market-coverage/events/) [Market Coverage](https://futurumgroup.com/insight-type/market-coverage/) ![](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/NP-headshot-no-jacket-cropped-e1725462619126-48x48.jpg) [Nick Patience](https://futurumgroup.com/author/nick-patience/) # Beyond Raw Compute: Equinix’s Strategic Bet on AI Infrastructure * [AI Platforms](https://futurumgroup.com/category/ai-platforms/), [Data Center](https://futurumgroup.com/category/data-center/), [Hybrid Cloud & Infrastructure](https://futurumgroup.com/category/hybrid-cloud-infrastructure/) ![Beyond Raw Compute Equinix’s Strategic Bet on AI Infrastructure](https://futurumgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Beyond-Raw-Compute-Equinixs-Strategic-Bet-on-AI-Infrastructure.png) Analyst(s): Nick Patience Publication Date: September 9, 2026 ## What Is Covered in This Article: * Equinix’s first Horizon customer event and its two flagship launches, Fabric One and Inference Exchange * How NVIDIA and Together AI fit into the Inference Exchange partnership, and who actually owns the GPUs * Why Equinix’s stock has swung from a laggard to one of the AI infrastructure sector’s strongest performers over the past year * What “neutral by design” means as a strategy, and where it runs into limits * How Equinix is pitching sustainability and community investment as part of the same AI buildout story **The Event—Major Themes & Vendor Moves:** Equinix held its first Horizon customer event on September 2 in San Francisco, following an analyst summit the day before, built around two product launches and a keynote pairing CEO Adaire Fox-Martin with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. Fox-Martin traced a lineage of neutral exchanges, from Mesopotamian trade clearing houses through the Athens agora, Amsterdam’s stock exchange, and Wall Street, positioning Equinix as their AI-era equivalent. She cited four forces reshaping enterprise infrastructure: compute fragmenting across an estimated 50 to 70 distinct providers by 2030, network traffic shifting from human-initiated to machine-to-machine, AI token costs becoming a board-level concern, and data sovereignty becoming a design requirement rather than an afterthought. Equinix says it already connects more than 60% of the Fortune 2000, across 282 data centers in 77 metros and 36 countries, with more than 522,000 interconnections between customers. Other Equinix executives put the same shift in economic terms: a typical enterprise already reaches roughly 20 clouds across six categories; within four years, that grows to around 50 clouds across 15, as neoclouds, model clouds, GPU-as-a-service providers, sovereign clouds, and agent-orchestration platforms multiply. Connecting to each individually, invoking Metcalfe’s Law, means costs that grow geometrically with the number of endpoints, an “AI cloud tax,” Equinix’s connect-once model is built to avoid. Equinix launched two products at the event. Equinix Fabric One is an intent-based connectivity service, built, Equinix says, in five months: customers describe a desired outcome rather than specifying routers, ports, and bandwidth manually, and the network configures itself. Infra & Chips.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # Qualcomm's Amazon AI Chip Deal Offers Momentum, Not a Threat to Nvidia [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Qualcomm has signed a multigenerational agreement to supply Amazon Web Services with custom AI data center chips and optical connectivity, with Amazon receiving warrants for 25 million shares at $161.26 each, a potential $4 billion stake. The deal covers up to $60 billion in purchases over 10 years and focuses on inference workloads, with revenue starting in the December quarter. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon views the agreement as confirming Qualcomm's existing $15 billion fiscal 2029 data center target rather than providing upside, maintaining a Market Perform rating with a $165 price target. By contrast, Rasgon rates Broadcom Outperform after the company projected AI revenue of $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. The partnership marks Qualcomm's second major hyperscaler win after Meta, but does not materially threaten Nvidia's dominance in AI silicon. ##### Key Elements ![Qualcomm's Amazon AI Chip Deal Offers Momentum, Not a Threat to Nvidia](https://img.biggo.com/JKwBbXNNyJHsu3qf4REzwHz38vOJmN9GvLxGb3L7vMI/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzEyYTAwMjA0LWM1NWQtNGMzNS04MTc5LTUzZDA2OGRjNWIyY18xNzg4OTg0MDA5X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Qualcomm has locked in a multigenerational agreement to supply Amazon Web Services with custom AI data center chips and optical connectivity, a deal that validates the smartphone chip giant's push into the infrastructure market but does little to alter the competitive landscape dominated by Nvidia. The partnership, announced September 9, sent Qualcomm shares up 3% as investors digested the terms: Amazon received warrants to acquire 25 million shares at $161.26 apiece, representing a potential $4 billion equity stake, according to a securities filing. The warrants expire September 3, 2036, and vest in tranches tied to commercial milestones and purchases of up to $60 billion in Qualcomm server chips and related technology over a 10-year horizon. The collaboration focuses heavily on inference workloads, the computational process of running AI models after they have been trained. Qualcomm said the effort spans multiple generations of custom silicon aimed at AWS's expanding AI infrastructure, with an emphasis on energy-efficient processing and system-level integration. Revenue from the arrangement is expected to begin in the December quarter. For Qualcomm, the announcement represents a second major hyperscaler endorsement in less than three months. Infra & Chips.content: [Skip to content](#main) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/ca/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/ca/) # AMD MI400 Ships With 432GB HBM4 to Challenge Nvidia [2026] * [![Marcus Chen](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/9fd5d0ea0dd03913800acb181fc9c69cee6db42ea45126b6e3b2a3445a6bb2fb?s=50&d=mm&r=g)](https://tech-insider.org/ca/author/marcus-chen/)[Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/ca/author/marcus-chen/ "Posts by Marcus Chen") * [Hardware](https://tech-insider.org/ca/category/hardware/) [Marcus Chen](https://tech-insider.org/ca/author/marcus-chen/) September 9, 2026 14 min read AMD’s newest data center GPU family is now shipping, and the specs make Nvidia’s own roadmap look tight. The **AMD Instinct MI455X**, the flagship of the MI400 series, packs 432GB of HBM4 memory onto a single accelerator, more than 50% above Nvidia’s current Blackwell Ultra B300. That gap, confirmed on AMD’s own product pages and repeated at Hot Chips 2026 in late August, has turned a once-lopsided AI chip market into a genuine two-horse race. For Canadian buyers, cloud operators, and anyone tracking where AI infrastructure dollars are headed in 2026, the AMD MI400 vs Nvidia Rubin contest is no longer theoretical. It is showing up in Toronto data centers, in AMD’s stock price, and in the cost of renting a single GPU by the hour. This piece breaks down what shipped, what it costs to rent, how the HBM4 memory squeeze ties back to the same shortage hammering consumer RAM prices, and what a Toronto AI inference cluster running Nvidia Blackwell chips today tells us about where Canada fits into this fight. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. The company’s own newsroom put it plainly: “Today at Advancing AI 2026, AMD launched AMD Instinct™ MI400 Series GPUs, the next generation of AMD data center GPUs engineered to redefine AI and high-performance computing (HPC) at every scale,” according to [AMD’s official announcement](https://newsroom.amd.com/news/aai-2026-mi400-instinct-update/). The launch wasn’t a surprise. AMD previewed the family at CES 2026 in January and gave a technical deep dive at Hot Chips in August, but July’s event marked the point where MI455X moved from slide deck to shipping product for cloud and hyperscale customers. The headline number is memory. Each [MI455X carries 432GB of HBM4](https://www.amd.com/en/products/accelerators/instinct/mi400/mi455x.html), spread across 12 stacks of 36GB each on a 2,048-bit interface, according to AMD’s product page. Bandwidth lands around 23.3 TB/s, though AMD’s earlier CES briefing cited a more conservative 19.6 TB/s, a gap that reflects refined binning as the chip moved toward volume production. Peak compute hits 40.26 PFLOPS at MXFP4 precision and roughly 20 PFLOPS at FP8, figures AMD says represent up to 4x the throughput of the prior MI355X generation. Those numbers matter because memory capacity, not raw FLOPS, has become the real bottleneck in training and serving today’s largest models. A GPU with more onboard memory needs fewer devices to hold a given model, cutting networking overhead and simplifying scaling. AMD is betting that a 432GB card beats a faster but smaller one for the frontier-model workloads hyperscalers actually run. ## Breaking Down the Chips: MI455X, MI430X, and MI440X The MI400 family isn’t one chip, it’s three distinct SKUs built for different jobs. Infra & Chips.content: ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/bigdatawire-logo.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### September 9, 2026 ### September 8, 2026 ### September 4, 2026 ## HP Extends Data-Center AI Architecture to the Edge *Enabling organizations to deploy and manage open, virtualized AI from the data center to the edge with HP ZGX Fury and Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA* PALO ALTO, Calif., Sept. 9, 2026 — [HP Inc.](http://www.hp.com/) today announced a collaboration with Red Hat, the world’s leading provider of open-source solutions, to give organizations more choice in where AI workloads run, whether locally, in the cloud or across both environments. In collaboration with Red Hat, HP is developing an open, enterprise-grade AI platform to deliver purpose-built AI infrastructure powered by Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/09/zgx-fury-press-release-header-300x121.png) HP ZGX Fury, powered by the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, helps organizations bring AI development, inference and orchestration closer to where work happens. HP’s open enterprise-grade AI platform aims to help companies maximize local AI inference throughput with up to 20 PFLOPS FP4 AI performance, reduce environment setup time and deployment risk, and improve GPU utilization through optimized NVIDIA CUDA libraries, scheduling, and multi-GPU workload orchestration. Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA is an integrated AI platform, built on the industry-leading infrastructure of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Red Hat OpenShift, for deploying and managing AI models, agents and applications across the hybrid cloud. The collaboration provides the ability to accelerate AI development by reducing setup time, enabling local agentic coding, and allowing companies to offload compute to the ZGX Fury without altering existing workflows. Running on Red Hat AI Factory, the solution is bringing together the co-engineered and jointly validated power of NVIDIA AI Enterprise and the scalability of Red Hat AI Enterprise. “The future of AI is moving closer to where people work, machines operate and critical decisions are made,” said Jim Nottingham, Senior Vice President and Division President, Advanced Compute and Solutions, HP Inc. “Together with Red Hat and NVIDIA, HP is extending enterprise AI from the data center to the edge with an open, enterprise-grade inference platform designed to give customers greater choice, control and consistency as they deploy local AI factories.” As organizations continue to develop AI solutions requiring AI inference closer to deployment sites, they must address latency, privacy, resiliency, data sovereignty, connectivity and cost. HP intends to help customers move from experimentation to repeatable production deployments with local AI performance and a consistent enterprise software foundation. The platform is being designed to support multiple AI workloads on the same system while maintaining workload isolation, governance, and operational control. This approach can help organizations improve infrastructure utilization and give IT teams a more consistent way to manage distributed AI environments. “Scaling AI from the data center to the edge requires operational consistency and reliability. By powering HP’s platform with Red Hat AI Factory with NVIDIA, we’re providing the stable, AI-optimized foundation businesses need to bridge the gap between IT and operational technology,” said Ryan King, Vice President, AI and Infrastructure Partner Ecosystem, Red Hat. “We are pleased to collabo...

Infra & Chips.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 1 minRead # Nscale, Figure ink US$3.5 billion AI compute deal with NVIDIA GPUs AI infrastructure provider Nscale has partnered with humanoid robotics company Figure for a multi-year AI compute deal, initially valued at US$3.5 billion and scalable to over US$6 billion. This collaboration could involve deploying 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs to support Figure's AI models and robots. The agreement highlights increasing demand for high-performance computing infrastructure in the rapidly evolving AI and robotics sectors. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Sep 08, 2026 at 08:50 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Nscale and Figure signed a multi-year AI compute partnership worth US$3.5 billion initially * The deal could lead to the deployment of 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs for Figure's AI models * Initial infrastructure deployment is planned for late 2027 in Barstow, Texas * Nscale will become Figure's preferred compute provider and take a stake in the robotics company [Nscale](/tag/nscale), a provider of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and high-performance graphics processing unit (GPU) cloud services, has signed a multi-year partnership with [Figure](/tag/figure), a humanoid [robotics](/tag/robotics) company. This agreement involves an initial commitment of US$3.5 billion in computing resources, with plans to scale the deal to more than US$6 billion. The partnership is expected to support the deployment of 100,000 [NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) GPUs as Figure expands the computing infrastructure behind its AI models and robots. The planned infrastructure may utilise NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform, the company’s AI computing architecture. Initial deployment is scheduled for the second half of 2027 in Barstow, Texas. ### AI Compute Infrastructure Focus The collaboration will see Nscale become Figure's preferred compute provider and also involve Nscale taking a stake in Figure. The computing infrastructure is designed to support Figure’s Helix AI models, which power its humanoid robots. The companies intend to integrate computing, AI infrastructure, and software across the model development process, from training through deployment. They will also explore the potential use of humanoid robots within Nscale’s own supply chain. Josh Payne, Founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Nscale, highlighted the growth in inference and agentic AI, stating that Figure is pushing the boundaries of AI. Brett Adcock, Founder and CEO of Figure, noted that the expansion of humanoid robots is largely constrained by data and compute, with their AI model, Helix, becoming more capable with increased data and compute. Jensen Huang, Founder and CEO of NVIDIA, commented on the emergence of physical AI through humanoid robots, describing the partnership as activating the robotics flywheel by training Figure’s models on NVIDIA Vera Rubin via Nscale’s AI cloud, validating them in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, and deploying them on NVIDIA GPUs in Figure’s robots. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?
